Kairos House

By: Stenette Grosskopf | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
A mentally disabled man goes missing form the home where he has been living for 11 years and no-one notices... as the search continues more and more is revealed about Kairos House

Unique Selling Point:
29 year old Shane Jordaan went missing from his place of safety, Kairos House on 4 June 2021. Event hough he had the mental capacity of a 5-year old, the management of Kairos House told no-one. It was only 5 days later that the family were informed by the police who were following up on a report of a missing person filed earlier that day. The family was devastated. Louise Jordaan, mother of 5, had a nervous breakdown and one of her daughters, Christan, took it upon herself to find out what happened to her brother. Numerous search parties were organised along with local security companies and dog units. Sadly the management of Kairos House refused them entry to the facility. Shane had not been allowed a home visit since the start of the Covid Lockdown, so the family had no clothes or items with his scent. They requested clothing from Kairos House to "train the dogs", they were refused. 29 days later, on the 3rd of July Shane's body was found 8kms from Kairos House. The autopsy report reveals devastating injuries, but no-one knows what really happened to Shane Jordaan.

Summary:
Shane's disappearance and death is suspicious. Kairos House is fenced, with razor wire and there is a security guard on the premises 24/7. There are various reports that a fight broke out between Shane, other patients and management on the day of his disappearance. When Shane was eventually found he was dressed in a different outfit as to what Kairos House said he was wearing on the day. To this day no-one from Kairos House has offered an explanation for what happened. They do not allow anyone access to the premises and they have not returned any of Shane's belongings.

But this is just the beginning... On 3 July when Shane's body was discovered on the R513, another patient, Gordon Cloete (48) passed away. Information from Kairos House says he died of natural causes. Autopsy reveal he had a bowel obstruction. On 29 July 48-year old Cornel Grobler committed suicide. She hung herself in the staff quarters of the facility. According to the security guard Frank van der Merwe she had attempted suicide twice before that. Her mother was never informed. In fact, her mom only found out about the death of her daughter from a WhatsApp by another patient. On 6 August, an anonymous patient passed away. She has been identified as Gabriella Hood and her death was confirmed by Bronwyn Engelbrecht DA(Gauteng). Engelbrecht has laid criminal charges with the Cullinan Police and Gauteng Province against the management of Kairos. On 12 August Peet Smith ran away from the centre and was hit by a car. He passed away.

Further information:
Many people have come forward about Kairos House and the state of the facility. There are photo's of the food given, which is basically coloured rice. This despite the fact that Kairos House receives over R4m annually from DSD. The owner is Susan van Niekerk (Babs). Her grand daughter runs many fundraising campaigns, including a Miss Kairos event annually to raise funds for the facility. Most of the "staff" who work there are family members, or related in some way. According to informants, Van Niekerk's daughter-in-law has a physical altercation with Jordaan the day of his disappearance. According to the security guard his arm was injured and he would not have been able to scale the razor wire fence as the management alleges. Photos of Jordaan eventually released by Kairos House reveal that he lost a lot of weight during the 18months of lockdown. Other families have come forward and said the same -- Deceased No.2's family have also mentioned that he was about 20kgs lighter at the time of his death compared to the last time they saw him.

Jordaan's family together with local security companies launched several searches in the area over the 3 weeks+ that he was missing. Kairos House denied them entry, except for a. security official who was escorted to the alleged point of escape... His remarks about the place was "'n gruwel-huis van semen en bloed"...
The filthy conditions at Kairos House have been corroborated by others. A previous winners of the Miss Kairos Fundraising pageant (who wants ot remain anonymous) was brought to the house to visit the patients (Dec 2019). She comments on patients sitting in their own urine. And that it was filthy. Photos of the sleeping conditions have been leaked by "Voice of Kairos" - a person close to the family who wants to expose the goings-on at the facility. Patients share rooms, sleeping on thin mattresses on the floor.

During one of the searches for Jordaan, security officers found a 20kg black tub filled with unmarked prescription medication just beyond the boundry fence. There are no other houses, facilities or people living nearby. Informants allege that patients are in charge of their own medication, or that sometimes fellow patients dispense the medication. The medication comes from Weskoppies, but at Kairos House itself there are no registered caregivers, nurses or doctors. During medical emergencies patients are taken to Mamelodi hospital for care, where staff have noted that patients coming from Kairos House are filthy and look uncared for.

Families comment that they often send new clothes and items for their loved ones at Kairos, but when they do see them, they are not wearing their own clothes, rather ill-fitting outfits that seem to come from a communal file. Families maintain that they get little or no information from management. And in the case of the patients who have died, none of their personal belongings were returned.

About Kairos House
The organisation seems to have been founded on 19 February 2014 as Kairos Bosveld Plesier vir Oud en Jonk by Susan and Johan van Niekerk. On 27 February 2014, a second company, Kairos Place of Safety for Young and Old, was founded by Susan van Dyk (same person) along with Gerhardus van Dyk and Neil Wesselo – Susan’s profession here is listed as “Visionary Leader”. In 2017 another company, Kairos House for Traumatised People was registered by Susan van Niekerk, Maria Nel and Neil Wesselo (Neil is mentioned in some Facebook posts).
There are several addresses linked with Susan and Kairos. Kairos House is situated at Plot 23 Elandshoek, Cullinan. Kairos Bosveld Plesier and Kairos Place of Safety are both registered to Plot 18, Elandshoek, Cullinan. Susan sometimes uses Plot 23, sometimes Plot 18 and sometimes Plot 34 Kaalfontein, Rayton as her address. Her postal address is 6 Suid Street, Rayton.
Kairos quickly became linked to the Mini Miss RSA/Little Miss RSA pageant, whose members raised money and held events for the residents. The most active members of this pageant are Drieka (Hendrika) van Staden and
Susan van Niekerk has also been director of Eagle’s Crest Lodge (along with Hendrika van Staden – presumably of Miss RSA). The company was registered in October 2020. Van Niekerk resigned directorship of Eagle’s Crest in August 2021 – after the allegations of several Kairos patients dying of neglect.
Van Niekerk was also the owner of Shammah House, for which Miss RSA has also raised money. On various websites, the same phone number is provided for both Shammah and Kairos, and some of the Miss RSA adverts say they are raising money for Shammah/Kairos. According to one article I read, Shammah was founded in 2010.
I was not able to find any company with the name Shammah House, other than a butchery situated in Siyabuswa, Mpumalanga. None of the various Kairos manifestations shows a change of name from Shammah to Kairos. But House Shammah is on Facebook with a picture of Susan and others as its profile. Their last post was June 2012. The page is linked to a website (http://www.experiencinggodministries.co.za/) which says it is a ministry founded in 2008. The address provided is Plot 45, Cullinan, and Susan’s contact details are there, along with those of a Kobus Kruger.
It appears that Susan van Niekerk is the mother of Hendrika (Drieka) van Staden and grandmother to Juanita van Staden. Drieka and Juanita also run Hennie’s Jolly Prawn, which I think is at the lodge. The Royal International Miss RSA is also held there as of this year. Hendrika is director of several pageant companies.
From around 2017, Kairos House became extremely active on Facebook, posting in particular numerous photos of the Mini Miss RSA pageants and fundraisers (see https://www.facebook.com/kairoshouserayton/photos/). This is up to December 2020 when the page went silent again.
Before 2020, there’s little online to suggest things were amiss at Kairos. However, the DA did in 2017 register a complaint against Shammah House for sending a lawyer’s letter to the relative of a patient, who had complained about ill treatment. The patient, Mike Thlolwe, was one of over 100 transferred to Shammah from Life Esidimeni in 2016 and died there in February 2017.
Shammah is mentioned a few times in the Health Ombudsman’s report on Esidimeni: as one of the NGOs not fit for purpose despite having patients placed and already being licensed; and as being not specialised in mental health but dealing only with poor and homeless people. Four patients were subsequently moved from Shammah in October 2016 to Bokang. The report also makes mention of patients being seen “in groups walking to the nearby shopping centre as part of rehabilitation […] the manager did not have special skills in psychiatry. It was merely the passion, experience and understanding of mental illness of the manager which contributed to the patients’ welfare.” The report also suggests that thanks to external funding, Shammah had greater financial stability, better staff satisfaction and better patient care.
In 2012, the Middelburg Observer also published an article investigating beggars standing at the traffic lights asking for money on behalf of Shammah. The journalist found that this was true, and Van Niekerk was assisting the patients to beg as the organisation allegedly got no funds from government, despite apparently being registered as an NPO.
Note that Shammah House did apparently feature in Tarryn Crossman’s 2018 story about Life Esidimeni and weirdly, Susan van Niekerk contacted us via web subs afterwards (see below). She was interviewed as part of the story.
On 10 February 2018, a Johanna Goosen (aged 65) died with her last known address being Kairos House, as reported in a Government Gazette. She had no surviving relatives. However, I have not been able to find out anything suspicious about her death. We could ask the executors of her estate.
However, things seem to have gone downhill pretty quickly, notably with the start of the pandemic.
On 4 June 2021, 30 year-old Shane Jordaan went missing from the centre. The centre didn’t notify the family – they learned of his disappearance 6 days later when the police phoned them. During a search party of 3 July 2021, his body was found on old Cullinan Road, 8km from the centre. The family believe it was dumped there after dying elsewhere. The family says they were not allowed to pack up his things – they were only given his SASSA card and his ID. They also say in recent photos he looked malnourished and ill cared for.
On 3 July 2021, 48 year-old Gordon Cloete died, apparently of natural causes. His family have questions about the medication he was given.
On 29 July 2021, 45 year-old Cornel Grobler allegedly hanged herself at the centre. She had been admitted for treatment for her depression in 2020. Her mother was notified via WhatsApp by another patient. She afterwards found out Cornel had attempted suicide before and she had not been notified. She was immediately removed from all groups and blocked; and was not allowed to visit Cornel’s room or take home any of her belongings besides her phone.
On 6 August 2021 an unnamed woman died. The DA confirmed the death. Her name may have been Gabriella Hood according to FB.
On 12 August 2021, Peet Smith was allegedly chased away from the centre by Van Niekerk. He left a suicide note and ran in front of a car.
The DA has laid criminal charges against the centre. The Department of Health has confirmed that a plan has been developed and an investigation is ongoing, due to be finalised in September. Two cases were opened at the local police station.
Shammah is still registered as an NPO even though it apparently should have been closed. I cannot find Kairos on the list, although there are many NPOs with the word “Kairos” in their names (http://www.npo.gov.za/PublicNpo/Npo).

Press Release:


A Place of Safety?
For almost a decade, 29-year old Shane Jordaan lived in a home for physically and mentally disabled people in Cullinan near Pretoria, but in June this year he disappeared without a trace. It was only five days later that his family received the devastating news, setting off a month-long search which ended in tragedy. Shane’s decomposing body was found just five kilometres from the care facility. The autopsy report revealed devastating injuries, but no-one knows what really happened to him. Now, more families are coming forward claiming that they too have lost their loved ones under suspicious conditions while in the care of this home.
Producer: Stenette Grosskopf | Research: Laura Byrne | Presenter: Derek Watts

Script:

The NPO Kairos House was founded by Susan van Niekerk and is managed by Neil Wesselo -- neither of them strangers to Carte Blanche. Shammah House, another care facility they run, was linked to the Life Esidimeni tragedy, receiving 55 patients from the Gauteng Health Department in 2016.

LIFE ESIDIMENI PART 3
Susan: I told them in August please take your patients. I can't deal with this anymore and then the next day they came back and said
they have nowhere to take these patients...
V/O
At least 144 people died from starvation, neglect and other causes in what is now called the Esidimeni tragedy. A judicial inquest to determine criminal liability for the deaths is currently at the North Gauteng High Court.
Shammah emerged relatively unscathed from the initial investigation. The Health Ombudsman’s report says the NPO was not licensed to deal with mental health patients, but its management’s “passion, experience and understanding of mental illness contributed to the patients’ welfare.”
But four years later, things seem to have gone wrong for Van Niekerk, Wesselo and their patients.

22’33

Ons het die soek en redding toe verder gesit in die huis waar ons afgekom het op ‘n boks tablette.
V/O
A large tub of about 20kgs of discarded medication was found, in an unlocked cupboard, in one of the rooms...
Bronwynn Engelbrecht
Why is medication found in an open container? Are they not being given the medication? Is it not being dispensed? Why is it lying around? A huge concern for me.
V/O
DA Spokesperson for Social Development in Gauteng, Bronwynn Engelbrecht, followed the case of Shane Jordaan closely...
Bronwynn Engelbrecht
Now remember the Health Department had been involved with the Esidimeni crisis, and a hundred and forty four patients had disappeared.
D: Sadly, very, very sadly.
So immediately, once again, it grabs your attention and immediately you think, Oh dear, what's happening?
LINK
The disappearance of Shane brought the community together. Many people joined the search giving their time and expertise freely. But apparently the people who were directly in charge of Shane’s well-being were nowhere to be seen.
Louise Jordaan
We couldn’t get any clothing, any bedding, to just give to the dogs to maybe get a lead of Shane.
V/O
On the morning of the 3rd of July the Jordaans once again met up with local security experts, hoping to find Shane...
Christan Jordaan
5’20” It was a normal morning. Me and my dad was on the way there, got a cup of coffee and...
V/O
As they walked along the R513, the Old Cullinan Road, the sniffer dogs picked up a scent…
Christan Jordaan
When I went the other side around I could only see feet but I didn’t know it was my brother.

Questions have also been raised about Kairos House as another four patients have passed on since Shane’s disappearance.

On the 3 of July Gordon Cloete passed away - according to Van Niekerk, it was natural causes. Three weeks later, on 29 July, Cornel Grobler died by suicide after she attempted to take her life twice before. … A week later, on 6 August, Gabriella Hood, or “Roxy” allegedly died by overdose. And on 12 August Petrus Smith was allegedly chased away by Van Niekerk and subsequently ran to his death in front of a moving vehicle.

Beyond the question of patients’ safety at the home, the alleged complete lack of communication with parents of the deceased is raising concerns.
Bronwynn Engelbrecht

Another parent was informed two weeks after the death of her child. So there's a lot of questions regarding the management of Kairos.
Marina Greyvenstein
Ek wil graag hê daar moet werklik voor ons weer ‘n tragedie het, iets gebeur...

Marina Greyvenstein is a retired social worker and active member of the local community. She’s concerned that Kairos seems to offer shelter to a mix of recovering drug addicts, disabled people and destitute pensioners...

Carte Blanche asks: just what is going on behind the closed doors of this care home?
text: Add New Proposal Shows Add New Show View All Shows 17 May 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 10 May 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 03 May 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 26 April 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 19 April 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 12 April 2026 - Carte Blanche HD 05 April 2026 - Carte Blanche HD Hi Lezanne [My Account] [Logout] Home Viewer Submissions Reports Contacts Music Cue Sheet Manage Users View Insert Edit Insert Insert Workflow Kairos House By: Stenette Grosskopf | Production Proposal Show: Carte Blanche One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): A mentally disabled man goes missing form the home where he has been living for 11 years and no-one notices... as the search continues more and more is revealed about Kairos House Unique Selling Point: 29 year old Shane Jordaan went missing from his place of safety, Kairos House on 4 June 2021. Event hough he had the mental capacity of a 5-year old, the management of Kairos House told no-one. It was only 5 days later that the family were informed by the police who were following up on a report of a missing person filed earlier that day. The family was devastated. Louise Jordaan, mother of 5, had a nervous breakdown and one of her daughters, Christan, took it upon herself to find out what happened to her brother. Numerous search parties were organised along with local security companies and dog units. Sadly the management of Kairos House refused them entry to the facility. Shane had not been allowed a home visit since the start of the Covid Lockdown, so the family had no clothes or items with his scent. They requested clothing from Kairos House to "train the dogs", they were refused. 29 days later, on the 3rd of July Shane's body was found 8kms from Kairos House. The autopsy report reveals devastating injuries, but no-one knows what really happened to Shane Jordaan. Summary: Shane's disappearance and death is suspicious. Kairos House is fenced, with razor wire and there is a security guard on the premises 24/7. There are various reports that a fight broke out between Shane, other patients and management on the day of his disappearance. When Shane was eventually found he was dressed in a different outfit as to what Kairos House said he was wearing on the day. To this day no-one from Kairos House has offered an explanation for what happened. They do not allow anyone access to the premises and they have not returned any of Shane's belongings. But this is just the beginning... On 3 July when Shane's body was discovered on the R513, another patient, Gordon Cloete (48) passed away. Information from Kairos House says he died of natural causes. Autopsy reveal he had a bowel obstruction. On 29 July 48-year old Cornel Grobler committed suicide. She hung herself in the staff quarters of the facility. According to the security guard Frank van der Merwe she had attempted suicide twice before that. Her mother was never informed. In fact, her mom only found out about the death of her daughter from a WhatsApp by another patient. On 6 August, an anonymous patient passed away. She has been identified as Gabriella Hood and her death was confirmed by Bronwyn Engelbrecht DA(Gauteng). Engelbrecht has laid criminal charges with the Cullinan Police and Gauteng Province against the management of Kairos. On 12 August Peet Smith ran away from the centre and was hit by a car. He passed away. Further information: Many people have come forward about Kairos House and the state of the facility. There are photo's of the food given, which is basically coloured rice. This despite the fact that Kairos House receives over R4m annually from DSD. The owner is Susan van Niekerk (Babs). Her grand daughter runs many fundraising campaigns, including a Miss Kairos event annually to raise funds for the facility. Most of the "staff" who work there are family members, or related in some way. According to informants, Van Niekerk's daughter-in-law has a physical altercation with Jordaan the day of his disappearance. According to the security guard his arm was injured and he would not have been able to scale the razor wire fence as the management alleges. Photos of Jordaan eventually released by Kairos House reveal that he lost a lot of weight during the 18months of lockdown. Other families have come forward and said the same -- Deceased No.2's family have also mentioned that he was about 20kgs lighter at the time of his death compared to the last time they saw him. Jordaan's family together with local security companies launched several searches in the area over the 3 weeks+ that he was missing. Kairos House denied them entry, except for a. security official who was escorted to the alleged point of escape... His remarks about the place was "'n gruwel-huis van semen en bloed"... The filthy conditions at Kairos House have been corroborated by others. A previous winners of the Miss Kairos Fundraising pageant (who wants ot remain anonymous) was brought to the house to visit the patients (Dec 2019). She comments on patients sitting in their own urine. And that it was filthy. Photos of the sleeping conditions have been leaked by "Voice of Kairos" - a person close to the family who wants to expose the goings-on at the facility. Patients share rooms, sleeping on thin mattresses on the floor. During one of the searches for Jordaan, security officers found a 20kg black tub filled with unmarked prescription medication just beyond the boundry fence. There are no other houses, facilities or people living nearby. Informants allege that patients are in charge of their own medication, or that sometimes fellow patients dispense the medication. The medication comes from Weskoppies, but at Kairos House itself there are no registered caregivers, nurses or doctors. During medical emergencies patients are taken to Mamelodi hospital for care, where staff have noted that patients coming from Kairos House are filthy and look uncared for. Families comment that they often send new clothes and items for their loved ones at Kairos, but when they do see them, they are not wearing their own clothes, rather ill-fitting outfits that seem to come from a communal file. Families maintain that they get little or no information from management. And in the case of the patients who have died, none of their personal belongings were returned. About Kairos House The organisation seems to have been founded on 19 February 2014 as Kairos Bosveld Plesier vir Oud en Jonk by Susan and Johan van Niekerk. On 27 February 2014, a second company, Kairos Place of Safety for Young and Old, was founded by Susan van Dyk (same person) along with Gerhardus van Dyk and Neil Wesselo – Susan’s profession here is listed as “Visionary Leader”. In 2017 another company, Kairos House for Traumatised People was registered by Susan van Niekerk, Maria Nel and Neil Wesselo (Neil is mentioned in some Facebook posts). There are several addresses linked with Susan and Kairos. Kairos House is situated at Plot 23 Elandshoek, Cullinan. Kairos Bosveld Plesier and Kairos Place of Safety are both registered to Plot 18, Elandshoek, Cullinan. Susan sometimes uses Plot 23, sometimes Plot 18 and sometimes Plot 34 Kaalfontein, Rayton as her address. Her postal address is 6 Suid Street, Rayton. Kairos quickly became linked to the Mini Miss RSA/Little Miss RSA pageant, whose members raised money and held events for the residents. The most active members of this pageant are Drieka (Hendrika) van Staden and Susan van Niekerk has also been director of Eagle’s Crest Lodge (along with Hendrika van Staden – presumably of Miss RSA). The company was registered in October 2020. Van Niekerk resigned directorship of Eagle’s Crest in August 2021 – after the allegations of several Kairos patients dying of neglect. Van Niekerk was also the owner of Shammah House, for which Miss RSA has also raised money. On various websites, the same phone number is provided for both Shammah and Kairos, and some of the Miss RSA adverts say they are raising money for Shammah/Kairos. According to one article I read, Shammah was founded in 2010. I was not able to find any company with the name Shammah House, other than a butchery situated in Siyabuswa, Mpumalanga. None of the various Kairos manifestations shows a change of name from Shammah to Kairos. But House Shammah is on Facebook with a picture of Susan and others as its profile. Their last post was June 2012. The page is linked to a website (http://www.experiencinggodministries.co.za/) which says it is a ministry founded in 2008. The address provided is Plot 45, Cullinan, and Susan’s contact details are there, along with those of a Kobus Kruger. It appears that Susan van Niekerk is the mother of Hendrika (Drieka) van Staden and grandmother to Juanita van Staden. Drieka and Juanita also run Hennie’s Jolly Prawn, which I think is at the lodge. The Royal International Miss RSA is also held there as of this year. Hendrika is director of several pageant companies. From around 2017, Kairos House became extremely active on Facebook, posting in particular numerous photos of the Mini Miss RSA pageants and fundraisers (see https://www.facebook.com/kairoshouserayton/photos/). This is up to December 2020 when the page went silent again. Before 2020, there’s little online to suggest things were amiss at Kairos. However, the DA did in 2017 register a complaint against Shammah House for sending a lawyer’s letter to the relative of a patient, who had complained about ill treatment. The patient, Mike Thlolwe, was one of over 100 transferred to Shammah from Life Esidimeni in 2016 and died there in February 2017. Shammah is mentioned a few times in the Health Ombudsman’s report on Esidimeni: as one of the NGOs not fit for purpose despite having patients placed and already being licensed; and as being not specialised in mental health but dealing only with poor and homeless people. Four patients were subsequently moved from Shammah in October 2016 to Bokang. The report also makes mention of patients being seen “in groups walking to the nearby shopping centre as part of rehabilitation […] the manager did not have special skills in psychiatry. It was merely the passion, experience and understanding of mental illness of the manager which contributed to the patients’ welfare.” The report also suggests that thanks to external funding, Shammah had greater financial stability, better staff satisfaction and better patient care. In 2012, the Middelburg Observer also published an article investigating beggars standing at the traffic lights asking for money on behalf of Shammah. The journalist found that this was true, and Van Niekerk was assisting the patients to beg as the organisation allegedly got no funds from government, despite apparently being registered as an NPO. Note that Shammah House did apparently feature in Tarryn Crossman’s 2018 story about Life Esidimeni and weirdly, Susan van Niekerk contacted us via web subs afterwards (see below). She was interviewed as part of the story. On 10 February 2018, a Johanna Goosen (aged 65) died with her last known address being Kairos House, as reported in a Government Gazette. She had no surviving relatives. However, I have not been able to find out anything suspicious about her death. We could ask the executors of her estate. However, things seem to have gone downhill pretty quickly, notably with the start of the pandemic. On 4 June 2021, 30 year-old Shane Jordaan went missing from the centre. The centre didn’t notify the family – they learned of his disappearance 6 days later when the police phoned them. During a search party of 3 July 2021, his body was found on old Cullinan Road, 8km from the centre. The family believe it was dumped there after dying elsewhere. The family says they were not allowed to pack up his things – they were only given his SASSA card and his ID. They also say in recent photos he looked malnourished and ill cared for. On 3 July 2021, 48 year-old Gordon Cloete died, apparently of natural causes. His family have questions about the medication he was given. On 29 July 2021, 45 year-old Cornel Grobler allegedly hanged herself at the centre. She had been admitted for treatment for her depression in 2020. Her mother was notified via WhatsApp by another patient. She afterwards found out Cornel had attempted suicide before and she had not been notified. She was immediately removed from all groups and blocked; and was not allowed to visit Cornel’s room or take home any of her belongings besides her phone. On 6 August 2021 an unnamed woman died. The DA confirmed the death. Her name may have been Gabriella Hood according to FB. On 12 August 2021, Peet Smith was allegedly chased away from the centre by Van Niekerk. He left a suicide note and ran in front of a car. The DA has laid criminal charges against the centre. The Department of Health has confirmed that a plan has been developed and an investigation is ongoing, due to be finalised in September. Two cases were opened at the local police station. Shammah is still registered as an NPO even though it apparently should have been closed. I cannot find Kairos on the list, although there are many NPOs with the word “Kairos” in their names (http://www.npo.gov.za/PublicNpo/Npo). For almost a decade, 29-year old Shane Jordaan lived in a home for physically and mentally disabled people in Cullinan near Pretoria, but in June this year he disappeared without a trace. It was only five days later that his family received the devastating news, setting off a month-long search which ended in tragedy. Shane’s decomposing body was found just five kilometres from the care facility. The autopsy report revealed devastating injuries, but no-one knows what really happened to him. Now, more families are coming forward claiming that they too have lost their loved ones under suspicious conditions while in the care of this home. Producer: Stenette Grosskopf | Research: Laura Byrne | Presenter: Derek Watts Script: KAIROS HOUSE SCRIPT FINAL V/O On the 4th of June 29-year old Shane Jordaan went missing here in Cullinan, Gauteng. Louise Jordaan 11’33” L: On the 9th of June the police contacted me and asked if Shane’s at home. And I said; No, why? Because Shane’s at Kairos. There must be some kind of misunderstanding. V/O Five days later his mother - Louise Jordaan - got the devastating news that her mentally and physically disabled son had apparently run away from his so-called “place of safety”.... Louise Jordaan 12’19” D: How did you take that news? L: It was shocking, because where’s my child? LINK This is the place that Shane Jordaan called home for the majority of his adult life... At the time of his disappearance he had been living at Kairos House for over seven years, and for the most part, he seemed happy here... Louise Jordaan Even when he visited, on a Sunday morning, early, when we wake up he’s fully packed, geared and then he wanted to go back to the facility. D: So he was allowed out for weekends occasionally? Yes he was allowed out for weekends occasionally. And then Covid strike, and then we didn’t see him. V/O Even though Louise and the family had no direct contact with Shane for eighteen months, they believed he was in safe hands... Christan Jordaan For 28 days it was a struggle. My mom, for 3 weeks she didn’t speak (crying). She was just laying there. So it was, it was difficult … V/O Shane’s sister, Christan, was determined to find answers despite what she describes as a total lack of communication from the management at Kairos House. Christan Jordaan 19’55” D: Did they give any reason why they didn’t contact the family at all after he disappeared? C: Uhm. Neil’s allegation or saying was he tried to phone once. D: Once? C: Once. But we took the records of everyone’s phones in the house. There was no missed call. No call answered. Nothing. V/O The NPO Kairos House was founded by Susan van Niekerk and is managed by Neil Wesselo -- neither of them strangers to Carte Blanche. Shammah House, another care facility they run, was linked to the Life Esidimeni tragedy, receiving 55 patients from the Gauteng Health Department in 2016. ARCHIVE EXCERPT: LIFE ESIDIMENI STORY LIFE ESIDIMENI PART 3 Susan: I told them in August please take your patients. I can't deal with this anymore and then the next day they came back and said they have nowhere to take these patients... V/O At least 144 people died from starvation, neglect and other causes in what is now called the Esidimeni tragedy. A judicial inquest to determine criminal liability for the deaths is currently at the North Gauteng High Court. Shammah emerged relatively unscathed from the initial investigation. The Health Ombudsman’s report says the NPO was not licensed to deal with mental health patients, but its management’s “passion, experience and understanding of mental illness contributed to the patients’ welfare.” But four years later, things seem to have gone wrong for Van Niekerk, Wesselo and their patients. Christan Jordaan 22’33 D: How many search days were there? C: Every day was a search (Derek: “Everyday!) C: …There were nights, 10 o’clock, we got a call; we just saw Shane at the SPAR. Then me and dad will get into the car during lockdown because it was you were only allowed out until nine, risking to get locked up to go search for Shane. V/O On the 16th of June the Cullinan community carried out a large-scale search, with the help of several local security companies Neels Stoltz Die oorspronklike inligting wat ons gekry het toe ons met die soektog begin het was dat hy oor die palisade heining geklim het. V/O Neels Stoltz and Chris van Niekerk from Braveheart Bio Dog Academy were allowed access to Kairos House along with the police. Neels Stoltz My eerlike opinie was ek kan nie sien dat hy oor daai palisade heining sou kon geklim het nie.. Chris van Niekerk Ons het die soek en redding toe verder gesit in die huis waar ons afgekom het op ‘n boks tablette. V/O A large tub of about 20kgs of discarded medication was found, in an unlocked cupboard, in one of the rooms... Bronwynn Engelbrecht Why is medication found in an open container? Are they not being given the medication? Is it not being dispensed? Why is it lying around? A huge concern for me. V/O DA Spokesperson for Social Development in Gauteng, Bronwynn Engelbrecht, followed the case of Shane Jordaan closely... Bronwynn Engelbrecht Now remember the Health Department had been involved with the Esidimeni crisis, and a hundred and forty four patients had disappeared. D: Sadly, very, very sadly. So immediately, once again, it grabs your attention and immediately you think, Oh dear, what's happening? LINK The disappearance of Shane brought the community together. Many people joined the search giving their time and expertise freely. But apparently the people who were directly in charge of Shane’s well-being were nowhere to be seen. Louise Jordaan We couldn’t get any clothing, any bedding, to just give to the dogs to maybe get a lead of Shane. V/O On the morning of the 3rd of July the Jordaans once again met up with local security experts, hoping to find Shane... Christan Jordaan 5’20” It was a normal morning. Me and my dad was on the way there, got a cup of coffee and... V/O As they walked along the R513, the Old Cullinan Road, the sniffer dogs picked up a scent… Christan Jordaan When I went the other side around I could only see feet but I didn’t know it was my brother. UPSOUND Derek and Christan... C: Hy was kop eerste en voete was bo… Ek wou eers nie glo dit was hy nie… D: I think we should leave.. Are you all right? C: Ja, net bietjie naar... V/O Questions have also been raised about Kairos House as another four patients have passed on since Shane’s disappearance. V/O On the 3 of July Gordon Cloete passed away - according to Van Niekerk, it was natural causes. Three weeks later, on 29 July, Cornel Grobler died by suicide after she attempted to take her life twice before. … A week later, on 6 August, Gabriella Hood, or “Roxy” allegedly died by overdose. And on 12 August Petrus Smith was allegedly chased away by Van Niekerk and subsequently ran to his death in front of a moving vehicle. Beyond the question of patients’ safety at the home, the alleged complete lack of communication with parents of the deceased is raising concerns. Bronwynn Engelbrecht 00:05:20:11 - 00:05:25:17 Kairos has been absolutely silent regarding this whole story. And that is not just with Shane Jordaan. The one parents whose child passed away was informed via an SMS. Another parent was informed two weeks after the death of her child. So there's a lot of questions regarding the management of Kairos. Marina Greyvenstein Ek wil graag hê daar moet werklik voor ons weer ‘n tragedie het, iets gebeur... V/O Marina Greyvenstein is a retired social worker and active member of the local community. She’s concerned that Kairos seems to offer shelter to a mix of recovering drug addicts, disabled people and destitute pensioners... Marina Greyvenstein Dit is regtigwaar ‘n resep vir.. Die Engels gaan sê “disaster” nê? Want die ouens wat onttrek van dwelms het spesiale aandag nodig, en spesiale medikasie nodig, en die psigiatriese pasient kan ander ouens onstel. V/O There are also allegations that Kairos House employs no trained care workers and that medication is often dispensed by the patients themselves. Bronwynn Engelbrecht One must remember that a lot of these people are psychiatric patients, so they get their medication from Weskoppies, which is psychiatric medication... V/O Engelbrecht has laid charges against Kairos Management with local & provincial police, as well as the NPA… but at the moment the Jordaan family is no closer to finding out how Shane’s body ended up in the ravine. LINK The post mortem report shows multiple fractures, injuries and blunt force trauma… but the most telling part is that Shane’s Body Mass Index was just 17.9 V/O At the time of death Shane was severely underweight… and photos leaked to Christan of Kairos House Patients in December 2019, shows that he had lost a significant amount of weight since his birthday in August that year. Christan Jordaan 14’53 D: It seems that Shane’s health deteriorated quite drastically … C: The last time we saw Shane he wasn’t on diapers, he was he was healthy, he was round, he was kind of a bit fat. Bronwynn Engelbrecht 00:13:17:18 - 00:13:51:24 I have been informed that the patients have been underfed. They've been exceptionally thin. The one patient lost 20 kilograms in one year... V/O Photos of the food served at Kairos House have also been leaked, and suggest that the patients are eating little more than flavoured rice. This also seems to be the case at Shammah House, van Niekerk’s second facility that was supposed to be closed down after Life Esidimeni. Marietjie Eendag pap, eendag rys. Dit bly dieselfde kos oor en oor. V/O Marietjie Weyers worked for Van Niekerk for a while - not at Kairos, but at the family-owned Conference Venue, Eagle’s Crest. Her employment deal included accommodation at Shammah for her and her son, where about 20 destitute pensioners are renting unserviced wendy houses from Van Niekerk. Marietjie Hulle kry byvoorbeeld skenkings van mense af. Daai kos wat hulle die skenkings voor kry word nie rerig vir die ou mense gegee nie. Daai kosse word uitgedeel vir haar families. Bronwynn Engelbrecht 00:21:54:09 - 00:22:13:16 A lot of companies that were donating stuff to Kairos have actually stopped donating. Apparently they have said that the stuff has been sold... V/O We tried to contact Susan van Niekerk, but she didn’t answer our calls or sms’es. We even left a message with manager, Neil Wesselo. UPSOUND Call LINK We’re driving into Kairos House. Susan van Niekerk hasn’t returned any of our calls or messages, and we have to get some answers. UPSOUND Derek & Susan D; We want to chat to you about the recent deaths here at kairos House. S: You’re welcome. D: Could we come through? S: yes you can, you’re welcome... V/O Van Niekerk phoned her lawyer and family for advice…. And the reception turned cold quite swiftly. UPSOUND Derek & Susan D: So Susan will you chat to us now? S: No. D: Why not? S; Because my lawyer said not. Because “daar is sake teen ons”…. V/O Van Niekerk insisted that she has nothing to hide, and told us Gabriella Hood, “Roxy” is in fact alive ... UPSOUND Derek & Susan D; Susan it seems you never communicate with the relatives… S: Because from whatever happened. I was just accused of everything. Nobody asked my story. Everybody just start accusing me of everything. And that’s why I got my lawyer D: And that’s as much as you want to tell us today? S: That’s as much as I wast to tell you today. D: Okay V/O Van Niekerk promised us an interview and access to Kairos House, sources told us that the facility was a hive of cleaning activity over the next few days. However, when we phoned her lawyer, Mr Oeloff De Meyer, he rejected the request for an interview, and did not respond to any of our written questions. Christan Jordaan 7’56 D: Did they give you any answers from Kairos house? Susan or Neil? C: Nothing, up until today nothing. Nothing. They don’t even want to speak to us. They didn’t even on the day that Shane was found, they didn’t even say sorry for your loss. D: Not a few flowers? A note? C: Nothing. Not even just a sms. *** PROMO 1 11” In June, a young man went missing from a care home in Cullinan, Gauteng. But this was only the beginning of revelations about alleged neglect and abuse at this so-called place of safety. PROMO 2 21” In June, a young man went missing from a care home in Cullinan, Gauteng. UPSOUND: CHRISTAN: There were nights, 10 o’clock, we got a call; Then me and dad will get into the car during lockdown risking to get locked up ... A month later, his body was found - but his family is still desperately seeking answers about his treatment in this place of safety PROMO 3 21” In just two months this year, five deaths were reported among the residents of a home for the mentally and physically disabled in Cullinan. UPSOUND: BRONWYN: I have been informed that the patients have been underfed. They've been exceptionally thin. The one patient lost 20 kilograms in one year… Carte Blanche asks: just what is going on behind the closed doors of this care home?

To this day no-one from Kairos House has offered an explanation for what happened. They do not allow anyone access to the premises and they have not returned any of Shane's belongings. But this is just the beginning... On 3 July when Shane's body was discovered on the R513, another patient, Gordon Cloete (48) passed away. Information from Kairos House says he died of natural causes. Autopsy reveal he had a bowel obstruction. On 29 July 48-year old Cornel Grobler committed suicide. She hung herself in the staff quarters of the facility. According to the security guard Frank van der Merwe she had attempted suicide twice before that. Her mother was never informed. In fact, her mom only found out about the death of her daughter from a WhatsApp by another patient. On 6 August, an anonymous patient passed away. She has been identified as Gabriella Hood and her death was confirmed by Bronwyn Engelbrecht DA(Gauteng). Engelbrecht has laid criminal charges with the Cullinan Police and Gauteng Province against the management of Kairos. On 12 August Peet Smith ran away from the centre and was hit by a car. He passed away.
metadata.Further information: Many people have come forward about Kairos House and the state of the facility. There are photo's of the food given, which is basically coloured rice. This despite the fact that Kairos House receives over R4m annually from DSD. The owner is Susan van Niekerk (Babs). Her grand daughter runs many fundraising campaigns, including a Miss Kairos event annually to raise funds for the facility. Most of the "staff" who work there are family members, or related in some way. According to informants, Van Niekerk's daughter-in-law has a physical altercation with Jordaan the day of his disappearance. According to the security guard his arm was injured and he would not have been able to scale the razor wire fence as the management alleges. Photos of Jordaan eventually released by Kairos House reveal that he lost a lot of weight during the 18months of lockdown. Other families have come forward and said the same -- Deceased No.2's family have also mentioned that he was about 20kgs lighter at the time of his death compared to the last time they saw him. Jordaan's family together with local security companies launched several searches in the area over the 3 weeks+ that he was missing. Kairos House denied them entry, except for a. security official who was escorted to the alleged point of escape... His remarks about the place was "'n gruwel-huis van semen en bloed"... The filthy conditions at Kairos House have been corroborated by others. A previous winners of the Miss Kairos Fundraising pageant (who wants ot remain anonymous) was brought to the house to visit the patients (Dec 2019). She comments on patients sitting in their own urine. And that it was filthy. Photos of the sleeping conditions have been leaked by "Voice of Kairos" - a person close to the family who wants to expose the goings-on at the facility. Patients share rooms, sleeping on thin mattresses on the floor. During one of the searches for Jordaan, security officers found a 20kg black tub filled with unmarked prescription medication just beyond the boundry fence. There are no other houses, facilities or people living nearby. Informants allege that patients are in charge of their own medication, or that sometimes fellow patients dispense the medication. The medication comes from Weskoppies, but at Kairos House itself there are no registered caregivers, nurses or doctors. During medical emergencies patients are taken to Mamelodi hospital for care, where staff have noted that patients coming from Kairos House are filthy and look uncared for. Families comment that they often send new clothes and items for their loved ones at Kairos, but when they do see them, they are not wearing their own clothes, rather ill-fitting outfits that seem to come from a communal file. Families maintain that they get little or no information from management. And in the case of the patients who have died, none of their personal belongings were returned. About Kairos House The organisation seems to have been founded on 19 February 2014 as Kairos Bosveld Plesier vir Oud en Jonk by Susan and Johan van Niekerk. On 27 February 2014, a second company, Kairos Place of Safety for Young and Old, was founded by Susan van Dyk (same person) along with Gerhardus van Dyk and Neil Wesselo – Susan’s profession here is listed as “Visionary Leader”. In 2017 another company, Kairos House for Traumatised People was registered by Susan van Niekerk, Maria Nel and Neil Wesselo (Neil is mentioned in some Facebook posts). There are several addresses linked with Susan and Kairos. Kairos House is situated at Plot 23 Elandshoek, Cullinan. Kairos Bosveld Plesier and Kairos Place of Safety are both registered to Plot 18, Elandshoek, Cullinan. Susan sometimes uses Plot 23, sometimes Plot 18 and sometimes Plot 34 Kaalfontein, Rayton as her address. Her postal address is 6 Suid Street, Rayton. Kairos quickly became linked to the Mini Miss RSA/Little Miss RSA pageant, whose members raised money and held events for the residents. The most active members of this pageant are Drieka (Hendrika) van Staden and Susan van Niekerk has also been director of Eagle’s Crest Lodge (along with Hendrika van Staden – presumably of Miss RSA). The company was registered in October 2020. Van Niekerk resigned directorship of Eagle’s Crest in August 2021 – after the allegations of several Kairos patients dying of neglect. Van Niekerk was also the owner of Shammah House, for which Miss RSA has also raised money. On various websites, the same phone number is provided for both Shammah and Kairos, and some of the Miss RSA adverts say they are raising money for Shammah/Kairos. According to one article I read, Shammah was founded in 2010. I was not able to find any company with the name Shammah House, other than a butchery situated in Siyabuswa, Mpumalanga. None of the various Kairos manifestations shows a change of name from Shammah to Kairos. But House Shammah is on Facebook with a picture of Susan and others as its profile. Their last post was June 2012. The page is linked to a website (http://www.experiencinggodministries.co.za/) which says it is a ministry founded in 2008. The address provided is Plot 45, Cullinan, and Susan’s contact details are there, along with those of a Kobus Kruger. It appears that Susan van Niekerk is the mother of Hendrika (Drieka) van Staden and grandmother to Juanita van Staden. Drieka and Juanita also run Hennie’s Jolly Prawn, which I think is at the lodge. The Royal International Miss RSA is also held there as of this year. Hendrika is director of several pageant companies. From around 2017, Kairos House became extremely active on Facebook, posting in particular numerous photos of the Mini Miss RSA pageants and fundraisers (see https://www.facebook.com/kairoshouserayton/photos/). This is up to December 2020 when the page went silent again. Before 2020, there’s little online to suggest things were amiss at Kairos. However, the DA did in 2017 register a complaint against Shammah House for sending a lawyer’s letter to the relative of a patient, who had complained about ill treatment. The patient, Mike Thlolwe, was one of over 100 transferred to Shammah from Life Esidimeni in 2016 and died there in February 2017. Shammah is mentioned a few times in the Health Ombudsman’s report on Esidimeni: as one of the NGOs not fit for purpose despite having patients placed and already being licensed; and as being not specialised in mental health but dealing only with poor and homeless people. Four patients were subsequently moved from Shammah in October 2016 to Bokang. The report also makes mention of patients being seen “in groups walking to the nearby shopping centre as part of rehabilitation […] the manager did not have special skills in psychiatry. It was merely the passion, experience and understanding of mental illness of the manager which contributed to the patients’ welfare.” The report also suggests that thanks to external funding, Shammah had greater financial stability, better staff satisfaction and better patient care. In 2012, the Middelburg Observer also published an article investigating beggars standing at the traffic lights asking for money on behalf of Shammah. The journalist found that this was true, and Van Niekerk was assisting the patients to beg as the organisation allegedly got no funds from government, despite apparently being registered as an NPO. Note that Shammah House did apparently feature in Tarryn Crossman’s 2018 story about Life Esidimeni and weirdly, Susan van Niekerk contacted us via web subs afterwards (see below). She was interviewed as part of the story. On 10 February 2018, a Johanna Goosen (aged 65) died with her last known address being Kairos House, as reported in a Government Gazette. She had no surviving relatives. However, I have not been able to find out anything suspicious about her death. We could ask the executors of her estate. However, things seem to have gone downhill pretty quickly, notably with the start of the pandemic. On 4 June 2021, 30 year-old Shane Jordaan went missing from the centre. The centre didn’t notify the family – they learned of his disappearance 6 days later when the police phoned them. During a search party of 3 July 2021, his body was found on old Cullinan Road, 8km from the centre. The family believe it was dumped there after dying elsewhere. The family says they were not allowed to pack up his things – they were only given his SASSA card and his ID. They also say in recent photos he looked malnourished and ill cared for. On 3 July 2021, 48 year-old Gordon Cloete died, apparently of natural causes. His family have questions about the medication he was given. On 29 July 2021, 45 year-old Cornel Grobler allegedly hanged herself at the centre. She had been admitted for treatment for her depression in 2020. Her mother was notified via WhatsApp by another patient. She afterwards found out Cornel had attempted suicide before and she had not been notified. She was immediately removed from all groups and blocked; and was not allowed to visit Cornel’s room or take home any of her belongings besides her phone. On 6 August 2021 an unnamed woman died. The DA confirmed the death. Her name may have been Gabriella Hood according to FB. On 12 August 2021, Peet Smith was allegedly chased away from the centre by Van Niekerk. He left a suicide note and ran in front of a car. The DA has laid criminal charges against the centre. The Department of Health has confirmed that a plan has been developed and an investigation is ongoing, due to be finalised in September. Two cases were opened at the local police station. Shammah is still registered as an NPO even though it apparently should have been closed. I cannot find Kairos on the list, although there are many NPOs with the word “Kairos” in their names (http://www.npo.gov.za/PublicNpo/Npo).
